passed through to dpl.xdate (corr, bin_floor and p_val are ignored when preset="COFECHA"; window_length still applies). slide_period= is a deprecated alias of window_length.

'spearman' bin_floor

passed through to dpl.xdate (corr, bin_floor and p_val are ignored when preset="COFECHA"; window_length still applies). slide_period= is a deprecated alias of window_length.

'spearman' p_val

passed through to dpl.xdate (corr, bin_floor and p_val are ignored when preset="COFECHA"; window_length still applies). slide_period= is a deprecated alias of window_length.

'spearman' output (both, screen, file)

where the full report goes: "screen" prints it, "file" writes a <name>.txt in out_dir, "both" does both. The report text is always in the returned dict regardless.

"both" verbose bool

print a one-line per-file progress note and a final tally.

True preset str or None

set to "COFECHA" (case-insensitive) to emulate the COFECHA program (see above).

None spline_period int

spline stiffness (years) for the preset="COFECHA" detrend and variance stabilization (COFECHA's 32).

32 name str or None

Report label for a DataFrame input -- the report title, .txt filename, and key in the returned dict. Ignored for file paths. Defaults to "report".

None

Returns:

Type Description dict

{path: {"text": str, "report": dict}} for files read successfully, or {path: {"error": str}} for files that failed.

References

.. [1] https://opendendro.github.io/dplPy/reference/crossdating/#xdate_report

docs.title: xdate_plot
docs.text:
dplR-style crossdating overview for a set of series (see corr.rwl.seg).

A thin wrapper: crossdates data with xdate() (same parameters; slide_period= is a deprecated alias of window_length) and draws the green/blue/red segment plot -- green = series extent, blue = a segment that correlates significantly with the master, red = a flagged segment (p >= p_val). Returns the matplotlib Axes.

Note: this plot shows only the significance screen (dplR's corr.rwl.seg, i.e. the A flag) -- red marks a segment whose dated (lag-0) correlation is not significant. It does NOT show the B flag (a segment that correlates better at a non-dated lag -- a possible dating shift), which dplR's plot has no concept of. A B-flagged segment that still dates significantly is drawn blue here, so it looks fine on the plot even though xdate() reports it as a problem. Always read the text xdate() flag report alongside this plot to catch B (lag) flags.

References

.. [1] https://opendendro.github.io/dplPy/reference/crossdating/#xdate_plot

docs.title: xdate_floater
docs.text:
Estimate the calendar dating of a floating (undated) ring-width series.

Slide the floating series against a dated master and score each offset by correlation, reporting the best-fit placement with crossdating statistics (t-value, effective df, Bonferroni-corrected p, isolation factor).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default data DataFrame or Series

The dated reference (year-indexed). A DataFrame is a collection of ring-width series, averaged into the master; a Series (or one-column DataFrame) is used directly as the master -- e.g. crn["std"] from dpl.read_crn. For an already-residual/prewhitened chronology, pass transform="none" to avoid prewhitening twice. Years with no measurement in any series are kept as NaN on the calendar grid (they are never dropped), and every offset is scored on its complete pairs.

required series sequence or Series / DataFrame

The floating (undated) ring-width series -- ring values oldest to youngest; any calendar index is ignored. An interior NaN is an unmeasured ring and keeps its position (it is not compressed out).

required series_name str or None

Label for the floating series. None takes it from the series itself (a named Series or one-column DataFrame header), falling back to "Unknown".

None min_overlap int

Minimum overlapping (pairwise-complete) rings required to score an offset.

50 transform (pw, fd, none)

High-pass transform applied (after mean-normalization) before correlating, case-insensitive: "pw" AR prewhitening (xdate.normalize_for_crossdating(), the package-standard autoreg._prewhiten), "fd" first differencing, or "none". First differencing sharpens the high-frequency signal but sharply reduces the effective degrees of freedom.

"pw" prewhiten bool

Deprecated alias: True -> transform="pw", False -> transform="none". Overrides transform if given.

None biweight bool

Build the master with a Tukey biweight robust mean (else arithmetic mean).

True corr (spearman, pearson, kendall)

Correlation used to score each offset (one-sided).

"spearman" ar_max int or None

AR order ceiling for transform="pw". The default follows COFECHA/ARSTAN (cap at 10); None uses dplR's floor(10*log10(n)).

10 first_aic_min bool

Select the AR order at the FIRST local AIC minimum (COFECHA/ARSTAN rule) rather than the global AIC minimum (dplR's ar(); set False).

True plot bool

Plot the sliding t-value against the series' end year, marking the best fit.

False return_rwl bool

Also return the floating series placed at its best-fit years (placed) and combined with the reference (combined).

False segmented bool

Also date each overlapping segment of the floater independently against the master and check that they agree (COFECHA UDATE-style). Adds result["segments"], result["consensus"], result["segment_candidates"] and result["internal_error"] (a dict describing a detected missing/false ring, or None). A coherent one-year step between older and younger segments flags an internal dating error the whole-series fit cannot see; at least four segments are needed for that verdict. The single-best-t placement remains the primary result.

False segment_topk int

With segmented, how many best placements to record per segment in result["segment_candidates"].

5 verbose bool

Print a short summary of the best-fit dating.

True

Returns:

Type Description dict

series_name; floater_cor_stats (a DataFrame with one row per offset, highest t first, columns min_year, max_year, r, t, eff_df, p_bonf, n); best (the top-scoring placement, incl. isolation_factor and one_over_p); and, when return_rwl=True, placed and combined.

Notes

Ports dplR's xdate.floater and adds crossdating statistics (t-value, autocorrelation-adjusted effective degrees of freedom, a Bonferroni-corrected p-value, and an isolation factor; Baillie & Pilcher 1973, Wigley et al. 1987, Wilson 2026). The correlation scoring reuses dplPy's crossdating internals, so results are consistent with dpl.xdate.

References

.. [1] https://opendendro.github.io/dplPy/reference/crossdating/#xdate_floater

docs.title: xdate_undated
docs.text:
Crossdate a set of undated ("floating") ring-width series against one another and assemble a single relatively-dated floating chronology (COFECHA UFLOAT-style).

Use this when no dated reference exists but the samples overlap in time -- e.g. a stand of sub-fossil or river-drowned trees. The series are positioned relative to each other and the earliest inferred ring is set to anchor_year (default 1).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default data pandas.DataFrame, dict, or list

The undated collection. A DataFrame is read as one column per series (its index only orders the rings, oldest first); a dict maps names to ring-width arrays; a bare list is auto-named S1, S2, ... An interior NaN is an unmeasured ring and keeps its position.

required transform (pw, fd, none)

High-pass transform applied before matching (case-insensitive): pw prewhitens (AR, via xdate.normalize_for_crossdating()), fd first-differences, none uses mean-normalized widths.

"pw" corr (spearman, pearson, kendall)

Correlation used to score every offset.

"spearman" min_overlap int

Minimum overlapping rings required to score a match.

50 crit_t float

A series joins the master only if its best t against the running mean reaches this.

4.0 anchor_year int

Relative calendar year assigned to the earliest ring of the assembled chronology.

1 min_isolation float

A placement whose leave-one-out isolation (the t gap to the next-best, well-separated position) falls below this is flagged for review.

1.0 ar_max int or None

AR order ceiling for transform="pw". The default follows COFECHA/ARSTAN (cap at 10); None uses dplR's floor(10*log10(n)).

10 first_aic_min bool

Select the AR order at the FIRST local AIC minimum (COFECHA/ARSTAN rule) rather than the global AIC minimum (dplR's ar(); set False).

True plot bool

Draw a placement chart (each series on the relative axis, coloured by isolation) with the mean floating chronology beneath it.

False verbose bool

Print a short summary.

True

Returns:

Type Description dict with:

pairwise : DataFrame of every pair's best match (series_i, series_j, lag, n, r, t) -- the UFLOAT table. offsets : DataFrame (indexed by series) of start_year, end_year, n on the relative axis (earliest ring = anchor_year). placed : DataFrame of the raw ring widths positioned on the relative axis. chronology : the mean floating chronology (Series on the relative axis). order : DataFrame of the join order with the join_t at which each series was added. verify : DataFrame of the leave-one-out check per placed series (loo_best_pos, loo_t, isolation, agrees, review). unplaced : list of series that never reached crit_t.

References

.. [1] https://opendendro.github.io/dplPy/reference/crossdating/#xdate_undated

docs.title: series_corr
docs.text:
Crossdate one series against the master built from all the others.

Produces (and, by default, plots) a moving correlation of the series against the leave-one-out master, the per-segment correlations, and a per-segment lag table (COFECHA-style) showing how the correlation changes when the master is shifted ± lag years past the dated segment -- an off-zero peak suggests a dating error in that segment.

Lag convention (lag_table and, by default, ccf): the dated segment stays fixed and the MASTER slides, so a negative lag means a missing ring in the series, as in COFECHA, dpl.xdate and dpl.check. The lag_table is xdate._lag_table(), the same scan behind xdate's B flags.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default data DataFrame

ring-width series (typically detrended RWI).

required series_name str

the series to examine.

required prewhiten

as in dpl.xdate() (window_length is the segment length; seg_length= is a deprecated alias).

True corr

as in dpl.xdate() (window_length is the segment length; seg_length= is a deprecated alias).

True window_length

as in dpl.xdate() (window_length is the segment length; seg_length= is a deprecated alias).

True bin_floor

as in dpl.xdate() (window_length is the segment length; seg_length= is a deprecated alias).

True p_val

as in dpl.xdate() (window_length is the segment length; seg_length= is a deprecated alias).

True biweight

as in dpl.xdate() (window_length is the segment length; seg_length= is a deprecated alias).

True lag

as in dpl.xdate() (window_length is the segment length; seg_length= is a deprecated alias).

True ar_max

as in dpl.xdate() (window_length is the segment length; seg_length= is a deprecated alias).

True first_aic_min

as in dpl.xdate() (window_length is the segment length; seg_length= is a deprecated alias).

True plot bool

master switch for drawing any figure.

True series_x bool

lag convention for the dplR-style ccf only (lag_table always uses the COFECHA convention). False (dplR's stock series.x=FALSE) calls ccf(x=master, y=series) so a negative lag marks a missing ring in the series, consistent with lag_table. True calls ccf(x=series, y=master), flipping the sign so a positive lag marks a missing ring.

False which (both, moving, ccf)

when plot is True, which figure(s) to draw: both, only the moving-correlation plot (corr.series.seg), or only the per-segment ccf panels (ccf.series.rwl). Case-insensitive.

'both'

Returns:

Type Description dict with keys ``moving_corr`` (Series), ``seg_corr`` (Series over bins), ``overall`` (DataFrame, one row for the series, columns ``rho`` and ``p_val`` -- the same shape as ``xdate()["overall"]``), ``lag_table`` (correlations at shifted master windows, lags x bins, using ``corr``), ``ccf`` (dplR-style Pearson cross-correlation per segment, lags x bins), ``ccf_bins``, ``bins`` and ``rwi`` (the transformed series used). References

.. [1] https://opendendro.github.io/dplPy/reference/crossdating/#series_corr

docs.title: interseries_corr
docs.text:
Mean interseries correlation (COFECHA's headline statistic).

For each series, correlate it against a master chronology built from every other series (leave-one-out), then average. This is dplR's interseries.cor(), and is distinct from rbar (rwi_stats), which averages the pairwise correlations between individual series.

Expects raw ring widths, not indices: each series is normalized by its own mean and, by default, prewhitened before the correlations are computed (the same transform as dpl.xdate, so the per-series values equal xdate()["overall"]["rho"]).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default data DataFrame

raw ring widths (as from dpl.readers), years as the index, series as columns.

required prewhiten boolean

prewhiten each series with an autoregressive model before correlating (autoreg._prewhiten, Yule-Walker, first local AIC minimum up to ar_max).

True biweight boolean

build each leave-one-out master with a Tukey biweight robust mean rather than the arithmetic mean.

True corr (spearman, pearson, kendall)

correlation type (case-insensitive).

"spearman" ar_max int or None

AR-order ceiling for prewhitening; None uses dplR's floor(10*log10(n)).

10 first_aic_min bool

AR order at the first local AIC minimum (ARSTAN rule) rather than the global minimum; ar_max=None, first_aic_min=False is dplR's interseries.cor.

True

Returns:

Type Description dict

mean -- the collection-wide mean interseries correlation (3 decimals, NaN-skipping); table -- a DataFrame indexed by series (in the input's column order) with columns rho (3 decimals) and p_val (one-sided); n_series -- the number of series with a correlation; too_short -- the names of series that overlapped their master by fewer than 3 years and were given NaN.

Examples:

>>> import dplpy as dpl
>>> res = dpl.interseries_corr(dpl.readers("series.rwl"))
>>> res["mean"], res["table"]
References

.. [1] https://rdrr.io/cran/dplR/man/interseries.cor.html .. [2] https://opendendro.github.io/dplPy/reference/crossdating/#interseries_corr

docs.title: Detrending & standardization
docs.text: Removing the biological growth trend to produce ring-width index (RWI) series. See the Detrending & standardization guide for when to use each method.

docs.title: detrend
docs.text:
Detrend a series or dataframe to ring-width indices.

Fit a growth curve to each series (a smoothing spline by default) and form the ring-width index as the ratio (method="ratio", division, the default) or the difference (method="difference", subtraction) of the data to the curve.

fit chooses the CURVE and method chooses the ARITHMETIC. This differs from dplR, where method selects the curve; passing a curve name to method raises a helpful error.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default data pandas dataframe or series

ring widths from dpl.readers, or a single series taken from one. Series with no measured values are dropped with a warning (a lone empty Series returns all-NaN).

required fit str or list

the growth curve to fit (case-insensitive; dplR's names are canonical): "Spline" (smoothing spline), "AgeDepSpline" (age-dependent spline), "ModNegExp" and "ModHugershoff" (negative-exponential and Hugershoff curves fit by nonlinear least squares, with a linear->mean fallback), "NegExp" and "Hugershoff" (the same curves by ARSTAN's deterministic fit), "GeneralExp", "LinearAny" (any-slope line), "LinearNegative" (non-positive-slope line, else the mean), and "Mean" (horizontal line at the series mean). A list of curves detrends by each and returns a comparison: a Series gives a DataFrame with one column per curve, a DataFrame gives a dict of them (not combinable with return_info).

"Spline" method (ratio, difference)

how the index is formed: "ratio" divides the data by the curve, "difference" subtracts it.

"ratio" plot bool or sequential

True draws one figure per series (the fitted curve and the detrended index) and leaves them all open under an interactive backend; "sequential" draws them one at a time, waiting for Enter between series; False (the default, as dplR's make.plot=FALSE for data frames) draws nothing. Figures are closed after display under a non-interactive backend.

False spline_period int or float

smoothing wavelength for fit="Spline" (get_period rule): a fraction of length in (0, 1], a percent-of-length spline if negative, or a fixed wavelength in years if > 1. None uses the dplR default (two thirds of length). The former name period= is accepted with a DeprecationWarning.

None nyrs0 int

initial spline stiffness for fit="AgeDepSpline" (see dpl.ads).

50 pos_slope boolean

allow a positive slope at the old-age end: for AgeDepSpline the spline may rise at the end, and for ModNegExp, NegExp and ModHugershoff the straight-line fallback may slope upward (otherwise a rising line is rejected and the series mean is used). dplR uses pos.slope=FALSE.

False f float

spline frequency-response amplitude at spline_period (fit="Spline" only).

0.5 verbose boolean

print, per series, the curve fitted and the arithmetic used.

False return_info boolean

if True, return a dict (like dplR's return.info) instead of just the data::

{"rwi":        the detrended series (same shape as the input),
 "curves":     the fitted detrending curves,
 "model_info": per-series description of the fit actually used,
 "data_info":  per-series {n_zeros, zero_years} of the input,
 "dirty_dog":  True if any curve went non-positive or fell back to the mean}
False

Returns:

Name Type Description data pandas dataframe or series

the detrended data, tagged attrs["kind"] = "rwi" and carrying the input's provenance attrs.

Examples:

>>> import dplpy as dpl
>>> data = dpl.readers("../tests/data/csv/file.csv")
>>> dpl.detrend(data)                     # all series in a dataframe
>>> dpl.detrend(data["SeriesA"], fit="ModNegExp", method="difference")
Notes

Interior NaN are unmeasured rings. They are left out of the fit and stay NaN in the index, but they still count as rings: the position-based fits (every curve except Spline and Mean) are fitted on the true ring position, so a gap advances cambial age rather than compressing the axis after it (AgeDepSpline carries the previous ring's value across the gap for its fit). Spline is fit over calendar years and Mean is order-invariant. To fill gaps instead, use dpl.fill_internal first.

A series too short for the requested curve (fewer than 2 to 4 rings, depending on the fit) is detrended by its mean with a warning -- dplR's "dirty dog".

References

.. [1] https://opendendro.github.io/dplPy/reference/detrending/#detrend

docs.title: rcs
docs.text:
Regional Curve Standardization of a set of ring-width series.

Align every series on a common cambial-age axis using its pith offset, average to form the regional curve, smooth it, and divide (ratio) or subtract (difference) the curve value at each ring's cambial age. This preserves the low-frequency growth signal that per-series detrending removes. Shares the fit / method / spline_period vocabulary of detrend. Analog of dplR's rcs.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default rwl DataFrame

ring-width series, years as the index and series as columns.

required po (DataFrame, dict, Series or None)

pith offsets: a table with series and pith_offset columns (or a dict / Series keyed by series) giving the number of rings between the pith and the first measured ring, so 0 means the pith is present. None assumes 0 for every series; a series missing from the table, or with an NA offset, is taken as 0 with a warning; negative or fractional offsets raise. (A dplR po table stores the cambial age of the first ring, where 1 = pith present, so subtract 1 first.)

None fit str or None

curve fitted to the age-aligned mean, from the detrend vocabulary: "AgeDepSpline" (default; age-dependent spline, honours pos_slope), "Spline" (fixed-stiffness smoothing spline), "ModNegExp", "NegExp", "ModHugershoff", "Hugershoff", "GeneralExp", "LinearAny", "LinearNegative", "Mean", or None for no smoothing (the age-aligned mean itself is the regional curve). Case-insensitive.

"AgeDepSpline" method (ratio, difference)

how each index is formed from the ring width and the regional-curve value at its cambial age: "ratio" divides, "difference" subtracts.

"ratio" spline_period int or float

smoothing wavelength for fit="Spline" (get_period rule): a fraction of length in (0, 1] (default 0.1 = 10%), a percent-of-length spline if negative (-10 = 10%), or a fixed wavelength in years if > 1. The former name period= is accepted with a DeprecationWarning.

0.1 nyrs0 int

initial stiffness for fit="AgeDepSpline" (see dpl.ads).

50 f float

frequency-response amplitude for fit="Spline".

0.5 pos_slope bool

whether the regional curve may rise at the old-age end. False keeps a non-increasing end, avoiding an artefactual old-age upturn. Applies to AgeDepSpline and the ModNegExp/NegExp/ModHugershoff linear fallbacks.

False biweight bool

build the regional curve with a Tukey biweight robust mean (else arithmetic).

True min_n int or None

truncate the regional-curve tail where by-age sample depth falls below this. Raises if no cambial age reaches min_n.

None preset (None, crust)

None follows the parameters above. "crust" builds the regional curve the CRUST way (Melvin & Briffa 2014): an age-dependent spline smoothed only where sample depth >= 4 with the no-rise tail rule, gaps infilled, a 0.02 mm floor, and flat tail extension. When set, fit/spline_period/nyrs0/f/pos_slope are ignored. Case-insensitive.

None rescale_difference bool

used only when method="difference". If True, rescale each series' difference index onto the mean and standard deviation of its own ratio index, so differences sit on the ~1 ratio scale. Default False returns residuals centred on ~0.

False rc_out bool

if True, return a dict with both the detrended rwi and the regional curve rc; otherwise return just rwi.

False plot bool

draw the regional-curve figure (series and curve vs cambial age). The former name make_plot= is accepted for now with a DeprecationWarning.

True

Returns:

Type Description DataFrame or dict

the detrended rwi (calendar-year indexed), or {"rwi", "rc"} when rc_out is True.

Notes

An interior NaN is an unmeasured ring: it advances the series' cambial age and its index stays NaN, so the years after a gap keep their true age (as in CRUST and dplR). Where no series reaches a cambial age inside the curve's span, the parametric fits use the true age axis and the splines carry the previous age's mean forward (with a warning).

References

.. [1] https://rdrr.io/cran/dplR/man/rcs.html .. [2] Melvin, T. M. & Briffa, K. R. (2014) CRUST: Software for the implementation of Regional Chronology Standardisation: Part 1, Signal-Free RCS. Dendrochronologia, 32, 7-20. .. [3] Melvin, T. M. & Briffa, K. R. (2014) CRUST: Software for the implementation of Regional Chronology Standardisation: Part 2, Further RCS options and recommendations. Dendrochronologia, 32, 343-356.

docs.title: sfrcs
docs.text:
Signal-Free Regional Curve Standardization of a set of ring-width series.

Ordinary RCS lets the single regional curve absorb some of the common climate signal when the sample's age structure varies over time, biasing the low frequencies. Signal-Free RCS breaks that feedback: it iterates, each pass rebuilding the regional curve from measurements with the current chronology divided out, while still forming the tree indices from the original measurements. Iteration stops when the chronology stops changing (tol). Port of CRUST's single-curve signal-free RCS (Melvin & Briffa 2014). The regional curve is built exactly as rcs builds it, so sfrcs(max_iterations=1) equals rcs (with the same curve settings) up to the signal-free normalisation of the chronology to mean 1.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default rwl DataFrame

ring-width series, years as the index and series as columns.

required po (DataFrame, dict, Series or None)

pith offsets (true offset, 0 = pith present), as in rcs. None assumes 0 for all; a missing or NA offset is taken as 0 with a warning.

None fit

regional-curve settings, as in rcs; used when preset is None.

'AgeDepSpline' spline_period

regional-curve settings, as in rcs; used when preset is None.

'AgeDepSpline' nyrs0

regional-curve settings, as in rcs; used when preset is None.

'AgeDepSpline' f

regional-curve settings, as in rcs; used when preset is None.

'AgeDepSpline' pos_slope

regional-curve settings, as in rcs; used when preset is None.

'AgeDepSpline' min_n

regional-curve settings, as in rcs; used when preset is None.

'AgeDepSpline' method (ratio, difference)

how indices are formed: "ratio" divides, "difference" subtracts.

"ratio" biweight bool

use a Tukey biweight robust mean both for the regional curve by cambial age and for the yearly chronology. Default False (arithmetic means) matches CRUST. The former pair biweight_curve=/biweight_crn= is accepted with a DeprecationWarning (if both are given, biweight_crn wins).

False preset (None, crust)

"crust" (the default, unlike rcs) builds the regional curve the CRUST way -- an age-dependent spline with per-point stiffness ss + cambial age smoothed only where sample depth >= 4, the no-rise tail rule, gaps infilled, a 0.02 mm floor and flat tail extension -- ignoring fit and its companions. None uses the fit vocabulary of rcs instead.

None ss int

CRUST's age-dependent spline stiffness offset (preset="crust" only).

10 rise bool or None

allow the CRUST curve to rise in its final third. None uses CRUST's rule (allowed only for curves longer than 1500 years).

None max_iterations int

maximum signal-free iterations.

40 tol float

convergence threshold on the maximum chronology change between iterations.

1e-3 rescale_difference bool

method="difference" only. False (as in rcs) returns raw residual indices centred on ~0. True rescales each series' residuals onto the mean and SD of its own ratio index, so difference indices sit on the ~1 ratio scale -- CRUST's residual mode (ind==2) and what signal-free difference indices need before the chronology is divided out, so prefer True for difference-mode signal-free work. (Before 0.9.0 sfrcs always rescaled.)

False plot bool

draw the regional-curve figure (series and final curve vs cambial age). The former name make_plot= is accepted for now with a DeprecationWarning.

True return_info bool

if True, return a dict of diagnostics (see Returns) instead of just rwi.

False verbose bool

print a convergence line.

True

Returns:

Type Description DataFrame or dict

the detrended rwi (calendar x series). With return_info=True, a dict::

{"rwi":        detrended series (calendar x series),
 "sfc":        the signal-free chronology (Series + samp.depth),
 "samp_depth": number of trees per calendar year,
 "conv":       max absolute chronology change at each iteration,
 "n_iter":     iterations run,
 "converged":  whether tol was reached within max_iterations,
 "rc":         the regional curve (by cambial age) that produced rwi}
Notes

Single-curve case (CRUST trc=1, src=1); multiple-curve signal-free RCS is sfmrcs. There is no dplR reference for this method: the port follows CRUST's stand.f90 and its spline smoother is validated against CRUST's compiled kernel, but the full iteration is not checked against a gold standard, so treat results as CRUST-faithful rather than machine-verified. An interior NaN is an unmeasured ring: it advances cambial age and stays NaN in the output.

References

.. [1] Melvin, T. M. & Briffa, K. R. (2014) CRUST: Software for the implementation of Regional Chronology Standardisation: Part 1, Signal-Free RCS. Dendrochronologia, 32, 7-20. .. [2] Melvin, T. M. & Briffa, K. R. (2014) CRUST: Software for the implementation of Regional Chronology Standardisation: Part 2, Further RCS options and recommendations. Dendrochronologia, 32, 343-356.

docs.title: mrcs
docs.text:
Multiple-curve Regional Curve Standardisation.

Sort trees by relative growth rate, split them into n_curves equal-count classes, build a regional curve for each class, and standardise each tree by its own class curve. This removes the modern-sample-bias slope that a single regional curve injects when the sample's growth-rate (or age) mix changes over time. Each class curve is built by rcs(), so mrcs shares its fit/method/spline_period/nyrs0/f/pos_slope/preset vocabulary, and mrcs(rwl, n_curves=1) is identical to rcs(rwl). Port of CRUST's multiple RCS.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default rwl DataFrame

ring-width series, years as the index and series as columns.

required po (DataFrame, dict, Series or None)

pith offsets (series and pith_offset; a true offset, 0 = pith present), as in rcs(). None assumes 0 for every series.

None n_curves int

number of regional curves. 1 reduces exactly to rcs().

2 sort (growth, age, diameter, none)

how trees are ranked before the equal-count split: "growth" by relative growth rate, "age" by cambial age, "diameter" by total radius, "none" keeps input order. Case-insensitive.

"growth" fit 'AgeDepSpline' method 'AgeDepSpline' spline_period 'AgeDepSpline' nyrs0 'AgeDepSpline' f 'AgeDepSpline' pos_slope 'AgeDepSpline' biweight 'AgeDepSpline' min_n 'AgeDepSpline' preset 'AgeDepSpline' rescale_difference

passed through to rcs() to build each class curve; see rcs(). Defaults match rcs(). The former name period= is accepted with a DeprecationWarning.

False reset_means bool

if True (ratios only), rescale each tree's indices to the mean it would have had under one-curve RCS, recovering the low-frequency variance multiple RCS removes. Skipped with a warning for method="difference".

True rc_out bool

if True, return a dict {"rwi", "rc", "alloc"} -- the indices, the list of per-class regional curves (by cambial age), and the series->class map.

False plot bool

draw the per-class regional-curve figure. make_plot= is accepted as a deprecated alias.

True

Returns:

Type Description DataFrame or dict

the detrended rwi (calendar-year indexed), or {"rwi", "rc", "alloc"} when rc_out is True.

References

.. [1] Melvin, T. M. & Briffa, K. R. (2014) CRUST: Software for the implementation of Regional Chronology Standardisation: Part 2, Further RCS options and recommendations. Dendrochronologia, 32, 343-356.

docs.title: sfmrcs
docs.text:
Signal-Free multiple-curve Regional Curve Standardisation.

Combine sfrcs() (signal-free iteration) with mrcs() (multiple curves): sort trees by growth rate into n_curves equal-count classes, then iteratively rebuild each class's regional curve from measurements that have had the current chronology divided out, while forming the tree indices from the original measurements, until the chronology converges. reset_means (ratios only) restores each tree's one-curve mean to recover the low-frequency variance multiple RCS removes. sfmrcs(rwl, n_curves=1) is identical to sfrcs(rwl). Port of CRUST's signal-free multiple RCS.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default rwl DataFrame

ring-width series, years as the index and series as columns.

required po (DataFrame, dict, Series or None)

pith offsets (true offset, 0 = pith present), as in rcs().

None n_curves int

number of regional curves. 1 reduces exactly to sfrcs().

2 sort (growth, age, diameter, none)

how trees are ranked before the equal-count split (see mrcs()).

"growth" fit

the regional-curve settings, identical to sfrcs() (preset="crust" by default; period= is a deprecated alias of spline_period).

'AgeDepSpline' spline_period

the regional-curve settings, identical to sfrcs() (preset="crust" by default; period= is a deprecated alias of spline_period).

'AgeDepSpline' nyrs0

the regional-curve settings, identical to sfrcs() (preset="crust" by default; period= is a deprecated alias of spline_period).

'AgeDepSpline' f

the regional-curve settings, identical to sfrcs() (preset="crust" by default; period= is a deprecated alias of spline_period).

'AgeDepSpline' pos_slope

the regional-curve settings, identical to sfrcs() (preset="crust" by default; period= is a deprecated alias of spline_period).

'AgeDepSpline' min_n

the regional-curve settings, identical to sfrcs() (preset="crust" by default; period= is a deprecated alias of spline_period).

'AgeDepSpline' preset

the regional-curve settings, identical to sfrcs() (preset="crust" by default; period= is a deprecated alias of spline_period).

'AgeDepSpline' ss

the regional-curve settings, identical to sfrcs() (preset="crust" by default; period= is a deprecated alias of spline_period).

'AgeDepSpline' rise

the regional-curve settings, identical to sfrcs() (preset="crust" by default; period= is a deprecated alias of spline_period).

'AgeDepSpline' method (ratio, difference)

ratio (division) or difference (subtraction) indices.

"ratio" biweight

the signal-free settings, identical to sfrcs() (biweight_curve= / biweight_crn= are deprecated aliases of biweight).

False max_iterations

the signal-free settings, identical to sfrcs() (biweight_curve= / biweight_crn= are deprecated aliases of biweight).

False tol

the signal-free settings, identical to sfrcs() (biweight_curve= / biweight_crn= are deprecated aliases of biweight).

False verbose

the signal-free settings, identical to sfrcs() (biweight_curve= / biweight_crn= are deprecated aliases of biweight).

False reset_means bool

restore each tree's one-curve mean (ratios only; skipped with a warning for method="difference").

True rescale_difference bool

method="difference" only: rescale residual indices onto the ratio scale, as in sfrcs() (needed for signal-free difference indices; see there). Before 0.9.0 the rescale was always applied.

False plot bool

draw the per-class regional-curve figure (make_plot= is a deprecated alias).

True return_info bool

if True, return a dict of diagnostics (see Returns) instead of rwi.

False

Returns:

Type Description DataFrame or dict

the detrended rwi (calendar-year indexed), or, with return_info=True, a dict with rwi, sfc (the signal-free chronology + sample depth), samp_depth, conv (per-iteration max change), n_iter, converged, rc (list of per-class regional curves that produced rwi) and alloc (series -> class).

References

.. [1] Melvin, T. M. & Briffa, K. R. (2014) CRUST: Software for the implementation of Regional Chronology Standardisation: Part 2, Further RCS options and recommendations. Dendrochronologia, 32, 343-356.

docs.title: ssf
docs.text:
Simple signal-free chronology (dplR's ssf()).

Build a signal-free chronology (Melvin & Briffa 2008): form an initial chronology, divide every series by it to strip the common signal, rescale and re-detrend the resulting signal-free measurements, and build a new chronology, repeating until the high-frequency chronology stops changing (the sample-depth- weighted median absolute difference falls below tol) or max_iterations is reached. Reproduces dplR's ssf(); for data with many absent rings that the basic method cannot standardise, use preset="crust" (see the note below).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default rwl DataFrame

ring-width series (raw), years as the index and series as columns. Series with no measured values are dropped with a warning.

required fit (Spline, AgeDepSpline)

detrending curve used at each iteration (the detrend vocabulary, case-insensitive): a cubic smoothing spline or an age-dependent spline (dpl.ads, fit with pos_slope=True as in dplR's ssf). Any other name raises. Before 0.9.0 this was called method=; a curve name passed to method is still honoured with a DeprecationWarning.

"Spline" method (ratio, difference)

how indices are formed: "ratio" divides series by curve, "difference" subtracts (the former difference=True flag, accepted with a DeprecationWarning).

"ratio" spline_period int or float or None

stiffness of the curve. For fit="Spline" it is the spline wavelength (get_period rule): None uses dplR ssf's 0.6667 of each series' length, a value in (0, 1] a fraction of length, a negative value a percent of length, and a value > 1 a fixed wavelength in years. For fit="AgeDepSpline" it is the initial stiffness nyrs0 (None = 50) and must be an integer > 1 -- a fraction is only valid for Spline. The former name nyrs= is accepted with a DeprecationWarning.

None max_iterations int

maximum signal-free iterations before giving up. Under preset="crust" it is raised to at least 40 (CRUST's limit), as difficult sites can need more than 25 iterations to converge.

25 tol float

convergence threshold on the median absolute difference of the high-frequency chronology between successive iterations (dplR's mad.threshold; the former name mad_threshold= is accepted with a DeprecationWarning).

5e-4 recode_zeros bool

recode zero ring-widths to 0.001 before processing (avoids div-by-zero from literal zero rings). The input frame is not modified. Note this does not help a chronology that is low but positive in a severe pointer year (the usual cause of a non-positive signal-free curve); use preset="crust" for that.

False return_info bool

if True, return a dict of the full iteration history (chronologies, signal-free measurements and curves, MAD vector, ...) instead of just the final chronology.

False verbose bool

print progress and the per-iteration convergence diagnostics.

True preset (None, crust)

None reproduces the basic signal-free method (dplR's ssf; Melvin & Briffa 2008). "crust" adds CRUST's robustness guards (Melvin & Briffa 2014): multiplicative rescaling of the signal-free measurements, the raw measurement kept in any year where the chronology is near zero (< 0.01), the fitted curves floored at 0.02 mm, and up to 40 iterations. These make ssf robust to sensitive sites with many absent rings (e.g. co021) that the basic method cannot standardise, and keep every series in the chronology. Case-insensitive.

None

Returns:

Type Description DataFrame

the signal-free chronology with columns sfc and samp_depth, indexed by year. If return_info is True, a dict of intermediates is returned instead (see above).

Notes

The basic method stops with an error when a signal-free curve goes to zero or below -- typically in a year dominated by absent (zero-width) rings, which drives the chronology near zero so that dividing by it inflates the signal-free measurements and the refitted spline dips below zero. This afflicts the whole collection at that pointer year rather than a few individual series (on co021, for example, trying to drop the offending series would cascade to nearly all of them), so ssf does not drop series; it reports the cause and directs you to preset="crust", which floors the curve and standardises such data with every series retained. dplPy's error is more specific than dplR's but stops in the same place.

References

.. [1] https://rdrr.io/cran/dplR/man/ssf.html .. [2] Melvin, T. M. & Briffa, K. R. (2008) A "signal-free" approach to dendroclimatic standardisation. Dendrochronologia, 26(2), 71-86. .. [3] Melvin, T. M. & Briffa, K. R. (2014) CRUST: Software for the implementation of Regional Chronology Standardisation: Part 1, Signal-Free RCS. Dendrochronologia, 32, 7-20. .. [4] Melvin, T. M. & Briffa, K. R. (2014) CRUST: Software for the implementation of Regional Chronology Standardisation: Part 2, Further RCS options and recommendations. Dendrochronologia, 32, 343-356.

docs.title: ads
docs.text:
Age-dependent smoothing spline of a single series (dplR's ads()).

Fit a smoothing spline whose stiffness increases with cambial age: the i-th ring is fit with an (nyrs0 + i - 1)-year spline, so young rings are smoothed least and the curve grows stiffer with age. Ports dplR's ads().

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default y array - like

a single ring-width series (no missing values, at least 4 rings), oldest ring first.

required nyrs0 int

initial spline stiffness (wavelength, in years) at the first ring.

50 pos_slope bool

if False (the default, as in dplR's detrend() and every dplPy detrender), once the spline stops decreasing its tail is held flat and the spline is refit, preventing an artefactual upturn at the end of the series. True lets the curve rise (dplR's standalone ads() default).

False

Returns:

Type Description ndarray

the fitted spline curve, same length as y.

Examples:

>>> import dplpy as dpl
>>> rwl = dpl.readers("../tests/data/csv/ca533.csv")
>>> curve = dpl.ads(rwl["CAM011"].dropna().to_numpy(), nyrs0=50)
References

.. [1] https://rdrr.io/cran/dplR/man/ads.html .. [2] Melvin, T. M. (2004) Historical Growth Rates and Changing Climatic Sensitivity of Boreal Conifers. PhD Thesis, Climatic Research Unit, University of East Anglia. .. [3] Melvin, T. M., Briffa, K. R., Nicolussi, K. & Grabner, M. (2007) Time-varying-response smoothing. Dendrochronologia, 25(2), 65-69. .. [4] Cook, E. R. & Peters, K. (1981) The Smoothing Spline: A New Approach to Standardizing Forest Interior Tree-Ring Width Series for Dendroclimatic Studies. Tree-Ring Bulletin, 41, 45-53.

docs.title: powt
docs.text:
Adaptive power transformation of ring-width series (variance stabilising).

Stabilise the variance of ring-width series by raising each value to a data-driven power p. For adjacent rings, level M = (x[t] + x[t-1]) / 2 and spread S = |x[t] - x[t-1]|; regressing log(S) on log(M) gives a slope b, and p = |1 - b| removes the level-spread dependence. Port of dplR's powt (Cook & Peters 1997).

Two methods are offered:

  • "cook" (default) estimates p independently for each series.
  • "universal" estimates a single p for the whole data set with a linear mixed-effects model (random intercept per year), matching dplR's default. Requires statsmodels; a log transform is used if the estimate is p <= 0.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default rwl DataFrame or Series

ring-width series (raw, non-negative), years as the index. A Series is allowed only with method='cook'. Series with no measured values are dropped with a warning.

required method (cook, universal)

per-series ('cook') or single mixed-model power ('universal'). Case-insensitive.

"cook" rescale bool

if True, rescale each transformed series back to its original mean and standard deviation.

False return_power bool

if True, return a (transformed, power) tuple; power is a Series over series for 'cook' or a single float for 'universal'.

False plot bool

if True, draw the data-transform-statistics diagnostic: per-series skew and spread-vs-level correlation, before and after the transform. A successful transform drives the after values toward zero.

False return_stats bool

if True, also return a per-series diagnostics DataFrame with columns skew_before, skew_after, r_before, r_after and power.

False

Returns:

Type Description transformed data of the same type as ``rwl`` (tagged ``attrs["kind"] = "rwl_powt"`` and carrying the input's provenance attrs). With ``return_power`` and/or ``return_stats`` the return becomes a tuple: ``(data, power)``, ``(data, stats)``, or ``(data, power, stats)`` (power first, stats last). Notes

dplPy reproduces dplR's power exactly. A given series' power can differ slightly from ARSTAN's, which uses the trailing ring as the level and clamps p to [0, 1].

Examples:

>>> import dplpy as dpl
>>> rwl = dpl.readers("../tests/data/csv/ca533.csv")
>>> pt = dpl.powt(rwl)                          # per-series (cook)
>>> pt, p = dpl.powt(rwl, return_power=True)
>>> rwi = dpl.detrend(pt, plot=False)           # transform, then detrend
References

.. [1] https://rdrr.io/cran/dplR/man/powt.html .. [2] Cook & Peters (1997), The Holocene, 7, 361-370.

docs.title: Input & output
docs.text: Reading ring-width and chronology files, inspecting metadata, and writing data back out. See the Reading & writing data guide for worked examples.

docs.title: readers
docs.text:
Read a common ring-width data file (.csv, .rwl) into a pandas DataFrame.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default filename str or path - like

a data file (.CSV, .RWL or .RAW). May be a local path (str or pathlib.Path) or an http(s) URL (e.g. from the NOAA/ITRDB archive) -- both are read the same way.

required header bool or None

whether a site-metadata header sits at the top of the file. None auto-detects it the way dplR does (any number of leading non-data lines, up to 3). False reads every line as data. True asserts a header is present: the auto-detected header is used, and when none is detected the standard 3-line ITRDB header is skipped anyway (dplR's header=TRUE).

None skip_lines int

how many of the first PHYSICAL lines of the file to skip before anything else (blank and comment lines count). The skipped lines are recorded on df.attrs["dplpy_skipped_lines"].

0 format (None, tucson, csv, tridas, pos)

force the file format regardless of suffix (case-insensitive). None infers it: .csv as CSV, .rwl/.raw as Tucson, .xml as TRiDaS, .pos (or a directory of them) as CooRecorder, any other suffix by sniffing content. ("rwl"/"raw" are aliases for "tucson"; "xml" for "tridas".) A TRiDaS file is parsed and, for the common single-table case, returned as one ring-width DataFrame; a multi-table or chronology TRiDaS file raises with a pointer to dpl.read_tridas(). A CooRecorder .pos file (or a directory of them) is read into one whole-ring DataFrame; use dpl.read_pos() for the full result (earlywood/latewood, attributes, coordinates).

None strict bool

True refuses a file with an unrecoverable problem (fail-loud). False (salvage) recovers as much as possible: a self-overlapping or precision-shifted series is dropped, a duplicate series ID is renamed and kept, and a file with nothing usable returns None. Every action is warned about and recorded on df.attrs["dplpy_salvage"].

True join bool

True (matching dplR) merges a series written as two or more disjoint same-ID blocks into one. False keeps them as separate series (the 2nd+ block renamed) -- the per-segment view a crossdating QA needs.

True encoding str or None

character encoding. None reads as UTF-8 (covers ASCII) and falls back to latin1 with a warning for non-UTF-8 bytes (e.g. an accented investigator name). Pass an explicit encoding to silence the warning. The encoding used is recorded in df.attrs["dplpy_encoding"]. Applies to URLs too.

None verbose bool

print the one-line success summary (file, format, series count, period) and the report of merged/split duplicate IDs. Advisories about the file (a truncated value, a short interior gap, case-variant IDs, an assumed encoding) are always issued as warnings, never printed.

True

Returns:

Name Type Description data pandas dataframe

Year-indexed ring widths, df.attrs["kind"] == "rwl". Non-fatal advisories about the file are attached to df.attrs: dplpy_beyond_column (first 50; total in dplpy_beyond_column_n), dplpy_interior_gaps (per series, year lists capped with n_ totals), dplpy_case_merged, dplpy_case_variant_ids, dplpy_blank_lines and dplpy_skipped_lines ({"n", "first"}), dplpy_encoding and dplpy_precision (plus dplpy_salvage in salvage mode).

Examples:

>>> import dplpy as dpl
>>> data = dpl.readers("../tests/data/csv/file.csv")
>>> data = dpl.readers("../tests/data/rwl/file.rwl")           # header auto-detected
>>> data = dpl.readers("https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/pub/data/paleo/treering/"
...                    "measurements/northamerica/usa/ak132x.rwl")  # read from a URL
References

.. [1] https://opendendro.github.io/dplPy/reference/io/#readers

docs.title: readers_url
docs.text:
Read a Tucson (.rwl) file directly from a URL.

Deprecated: readers() accepts an http(s) URL directly, so dpl.readers(url) does the same thing. This thin wrapper is kept for backward compatibility: it emits a DeprecationWarning and forwards every keyword (header, skip_lines, strict, join, encoding, format, verbose) to readers.

docs.title: metadata
docs.text:
Extract site/sample metadata from a Tucson (.rwl) file's header.

Returns a dict with best-effort fields (site_id, site_name, species_code, species_name, country_region, elevation_m, latitude, longitude, first_year, last_year, investigators) plus n_header_lines and the raw header lines. Unreadable fields are None. Reads only the header, so it is cheap and independent of loading the data; accepts a local path (str or pathlib.Path) or an http(s) URL. header and skip_lines mean what they mean in readers() (skip_lines counts physical lines). The same result is captured at read time on df.attrs['dplpy_metadata'].

docs.title: read_crn
docs.text:
Read a Tucson (.crn) chronology file into a DataFrame.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default filename str or path - like

Path (or http/https URL) to a .crn chronology file. Standard single chronologies and combined multi-block files (stacked ARSTAN types, or many sites concatenated) are both handled, as are BC chronologies in dplR's layout (a 5-character site ID with the year's sign in column 6).

required strict bool

True (the default) refuses a file with no readable chronology; False returns None instead. (Individual malformed rows are skipped with a warning either way.)

True split_by_site bool

If True, return a dict mapping each site ID to its own DataFrame (each framed as a single-site file: value columns named by chronology type plus a shared samp_depth). Useful for multi-site bundles, where the default single wide frame is unwieldy. A single-site file yields a one-entry dict.

False verbose bool

print the one-line success summary. Advisories are warnings regardless.

True

Returns:

Type Description pandas.DataFrame or dict of pandas.DataFrame

By default one DataFrame indexed by year: one value column per chronology (named by chronology type for a single-site file, e.g. 'std'/'res'/'ars'; by site, or 'site.type', for a multi-site file), index values divided by 1000 and 9990 mapped to NaN, with sample depths as 'samp_depth' (shared when several chronologies carry identical depth) or ' samp_depth' otherwise. With split_by_site=True, a dict {site_id: DataFrame}. df.attrs carries kind == "crn", dplpy_crn (a summary) and dplpy_crn_stats (embedded statistics lines).

Examples:

>>> dpl.read_crn("ga004.crn")
>>> dpl.read_crn("celaque_prelim_v01.rwl_crns.txt")
>>> by_site = dpl.read_crn("ALL.CRNS", split_by_site=True)   # {site: DataFrame}
References

.. [1] https://opendendro.github.io/dplPy/reference/io/#read_crn

docs.title: read_ids
docs.text:
Derive tree and core IDs from series names (site-tree-core convention).

Split each series name into a tree identifier (site + tree number, so trees and sites never collide) and a core designator, and return the mapping dpl.rwi_stats() and dpl.sss() use to know which cores belong to the same tree. Two parsing modes: the pattern default (stc=None) splits on letter/digit boundaries (leading letters = site, first digit run = tree, trailing characters = core); an STC mask (stc=(site_len, tree_len[, core_len])) splits by fixed character positions.

IMPORTANT: the pattern default cannot detect a DIGIT core. A name like "CAM031" is read as tree "031" with an empty core (no warning), leaving "CAM031" and "CAM032" as separate trees instead of grouping them under "CAM03". For digit cores, or site codes that contain digits, supply an explicit stc mask (e.g. stc=(3, 2, 1) for "CAM031").

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default data pandas dataframe or iterable of str

a dataframe whose column names are the series names (e.g. from dpl.readers()), or any iterable of series-name strings.

required stc tuple of int, or None

None to use the pattern default; otherwise a (site_len, tree_len) or (site_len, tree_len, core_len) character mask.

None

Returns:

Name Type Description ids pandas dataframe indexed by series name, with columns 'tree' and

'core'. Pass this directly as the ids argument of dpl.rwi_stats(), dpl.rwi_stats_running(), or dpl.sss().

Examples:

>>> import dplpy as dpl
>>> data = dpl.readers("../tests/data/csv/file.csv")
>>> ids = dpl.read_ids(data)                 # letter-core names
>>> ids = dpl.read_ids(data, stc=(3, 2, 1))  # digit-core names (e.g. CAM031)
>>> dpl.rwi_stats(dpl.detrend(data, plot=False), ids=ids)
References

.. [1] https://rdrr.io/cran/dplR/man/read.ids.html

docs.title: combine_rwl
docs.text:
Combine ring-width datasets on the union of their years (dplR combine.rwl).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default x pandas.DataFrame or list/tuple of DataFrames

Either the first dataset (with y the second), or a list/tuple of datasets to combine in order.

required y DataFrame

The second dataset, when x is a single DataFrame.

None warn_duplicates bool

Emit a warning if the combined frame ends up with duplicate series names (the columns are still kept, matching dplR -- this only flags them).

True

Returns:

Type Description DataFrame

All series side by side, indexed by a contiguous year range spanning the earliest to the latest year of the inputs (years with no data are NaN). attrs are carried from the first input (kind == "rwl"); the per-series dplpy_precision dicts of all inputs are merged.

Notes

Series columns are concatenated as-is: like dplR, duplicate series IDs are neither merged nor renamed. Deduplicate or rename beforehand if that matters for your workflow.

docs.title: writers
docs.text:
Output dplpy datasets to .csv, .rwl, .crn, .txt and .tridas (.xml) files.

Write a dataframe to a file as set by format, created in the current directory unless a path is included in label. For 'csv'/'rwl', data is a ring-width dataframe (years x series); for 'crn', data is a chronology (from dpl.chron()) and a header of site metadata is REQUIRED to populate the Tucson .crn header.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default data pandas dataframe

ring widths (csv/rwl) or a chronology from dpl.chron() (crn).

required label str

name (can include file path) to give the file; no extension.

required format str

'csv', 'rwl', 'crn', 'txt' or 'tridas' (case-insensitive).

required header dict or SiteMetadata, required for format='crn'

site metadata with the keys: 'site_id', 'site_name', 'species_code', 'state_country', 'species', 'elevation', 'latitude', 'longitude', 'investigators'; optionally 'completion_date'. First/last year are taken from the chronology. Coordinates may be decimal degrees (packed to the ITRDB DDMM/DDDMM field) or already-packed strings; elevation in metres.

None chronology_type str

for format='crn', the ITRDB chronology type written in header record 2: 'standard' (blank code), 'arstan' ('A'), or 'residual' ('R').

'standard' column str

for format='crn', which chronology column to write (e.g. 'std', 'res').

'std' prec float or None

for format='rwl'/'tridas', the measurement precision in mm. None uses the precision the data were read at (df.attrs["dplpy_precision"]; mixed precisions raise, pass prec explicitly), else 0.001 for rwl (values x1000, end marker -9999; 0.01 writes x100 with a 999 marker, the dplR mapping) and unrounded millimetres for tridas.

None gaps (int, split)

for format='rwl', how to encode a true interior gap (a NaN inside a series; a real 0 is a locally absent ring and is always written as 0): a negative integer (default -99) writes that sentinel in the gap (it must be negative so it is not read as a ring width, and not a stop marker; the reader turns it back into NaN), or "split" closes the block with the end marker and reopens a new block at the next present year.

int sep

for format='txt', the column delimiter (default tab), printf float format (default '%.4f', None for full precision), and missing-value text (default 'NA'). For 'txt', data may be a DataFrame, a single Series, or a list of year-aligned Series.

'\t' float_format

for format='txt', the column delimiter (default tab), printf float format (default '%.4f', None for full precision), and missing-value text (default 'NA'). For 'txt', data may be a DataFrame, a single Series, or a list of year-aligned Series.

'\t' na_rep

for format='txt', the column delimiter (default tab), printf float format (default '%.4f', None for full precision), and missing-value text (default 'NA'). For 'txt', data may be a DataFrame, a single Series, or a list of year-aligned Series.

'\t'

Returns:

Type Description str

the path of the file written.

References

.. [1] https://opendendro.github.io/dplPy/reference/io/#writers

docs.title: summary
docs.text:
Summarize a ring-width dataset.

Reports per-series summary information for a dataframe of tree-ring widths.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default inp str or pandas dataframe

a data file (.CSV or .RWL) or a pandas dataframe imported from dpl.readers().

required

Returns:

Name Type Description data pandas dataframe

Examples:

>>> import dplpy as dpl
>>> data = dpl.readers("../tests/data/csv/file.csv")
>>> dpl.summary(data)
References

.. [1] https://opendendro.github.io/dplPy/reference/io/#summary

docs.title: report
docs.text:
Generates a report

Extended Summary

Generates a text report about the input dataset that includes: Number of dated series Number of measurements Avg series length (years) Range (total years) Span (start-end year) Mean (Standard Deviation) series intercorrelation Mean (Standard Deviation) AR1 Years with locally absent rings (zero values), with per-series and total counts Years with internal NA (missing measurements), with per-series and total counts

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default inp str or pandas dataframe

a data file (.CSV or .RWL) or a pandas dataframe imported from dpl.readers().

required

Returns:

Type Description DataFrame

the per-series statistics table the report is built from (the output of dpl.stats()), so the printed report is also available as data.

Examples:

>>> import dplpy as dpl
>>> data = dpl.readers("../tests/data/csv/file.csv")
>>> dpl.report(data)
References

.. [1] https://opendendro.github.io/dplPy/reference/io/#report

docs.title: check
docs.text:
Check a ring-width collection for defects, reported as a table of findings.

The data counterpart to report(): report prints what a file looks like, check returns what is wrong with it, one row per finding. Every finding carries a stable check id and a severity ("error", "warning", "note"). Analog of dplR 1.8.0's rwl.check.

The crossdating group slides the leave-one-out master past each series over -lag..+lag (xdate._lag_table()), so a RWL_DATING_LAG with a NEGATIVE lag means a MISSING ring in the series, as in COFECHA, xdate and series_corr.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default x pandas.DataFrame, str, or list of str

a ring-width collection (readers output), a path to a Tucson file, or a list of paths / a directory for an archive sweep.

required file str or None

label for the file column when x is a DataFrame.

None checks list of str or None

which groups to run. Default all: structure, series, values, zeros, crossdating, file, provenance.

None summary bool

if True, return one row per file (counts per check and per severity) instead of the findings. pd.concat these over an archive to rank it.

False min_depth int 2 depth_run int 2 min_length int 2 run_min int 2 lag int 2 min_overlap int 2 spline_period int 2 r_dating float 0.35 r_margin float 0.35 outlier_mad float 0.35 outlier_gap float 0.35 r_cohesion float 0.35 plausible_mean float 0.35 small_thresh Optional[float]

tunables; defaults follow dplR's rwl.check.control except lag (10, dplPy's package-wide lag search) and spline_period (32, the high-pass spline). lag_max= and spline_nyrs= are accepted as deprecated aliases.

None big_thresh Optional[float]

tunables; defaults follow dplR's rwl.check.control except lag (10, dplPy's package-wide lag search) and spline_period (32, the high-pass spline). lag_max= and spline_nyrs= are accepted as deprecated aliases.

None max_year Optional[float]

tunables; defaults follow dplR's rwl.check.control except lag (10, dplPy's package-wide lag search) and spline_period (32, the high-pass spline). lag_max= and spline_nyrs= are accepted as deprecated aliases.

None

Returns:

Type Description DataFrame

the findings (columns file, check, severity, group, series, year_from, year_to, n, value, message), or, with summary=True, one row per file.

Notes

Every check group runs inside a guard: an exception inside a group (or in reading the file) is converted to a RWL_CHECK_ERROR finding carrying the error text, so one failing check never hides the others' findings and a sweep over an archive never stops on one bad file (audit G4). Check the engine group of the result to see whether anything failed to run. A misdated series may draw both RWL_DATING_LAG and RWL_SERIES_OUTLIER (its lag-0 correlation is low because of the lag); both are kept.

References

.. [1] Bunn, A. G. (2026) dplR 1.8.0, rwl.check.

docs.title: SiteMetadata
docs.text:
Site/sample metadata shared by dplPy's file exporters.

Field names mirror dpl.metadata() / df.attrs['dplpy_metadata']. Use from_rwl() to auto-fill from a frame read by dpl.readers(), from_metadata() from a metadata dict, or construct one directly and set fields by hand. to_crn_header() renders the dict the Tucson .crn writer expects (which uses a few different key names). Coordinates are decimal degrees and elevation is metres; the .crn writer packs them into the ITRDB fields (DDMM / DDDMM, "%dM") itself.

docs.title: from_metadata classmethod
docs.text:
from_metadata(meta: dict) -> SiteMetadata

Build from a metadata dict (dpl.metadata() output or the same shape). Unknown keys (e.g. n_header_lines) are ignored.

docs.title: from_rwl classmethod
docs.text:
from_rwl(data) -> SiteMetadata

Build from a frame read by dpl.readers() (uses df.attrs['dplpy_metadata']), or from a metadata dict directly.

docs.title: coerce classmethod
docs.text:
coerce(obj) -> SiteMetadata

Return obj if it is already a SiteMetadata, or build one from a metadata dict. Used by writers so they accept either form.

docs.title: to_crn_header
docs.text:
to_crn_header() -> dict

Render the header dict the Tucson .crn writer expects. The writer uses a few different key names (state_country/species/ elevation); this maps them. Values are passed through unchanged (decimal degrees, metres); write_crn packs them into the ITRDB fields via pack_crn_coordinates() / pack_crn_elevation(). Fields that are None are omitted, so the writer's own "missing required key" check reports what still needs filling rather than writing the literal 'None'.

docs.title: read_tridas
docs.text:
Read a TRiDaS (Tree Ring Data Standard) XML file.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default filename str

path to a .xml TRiDaS file.

required warn_units bool

warn when a measurement series uses a variable that is not a width in a length unit (e.g. a density), which dplPy does not convert to mm. Such series are kept out of the ring-width tables.

True

Returns:

Type Description TridasProject

A typed container: .measurements (ring-width tables), .derived (chronologies), .undated (floating series), .metadata. For the common single-table file, dpl.readers() returns the ring-width DataFrame directly instead.

Notes

Missing values become NaN (not 0); units are converted to millimetres; years use the dplPy continuous integer axis. See dev/tridas_design_2026-10-14.md for the full design.

References

.. [1] Jansma, Brewer & Zandhuis (2010), Dendrochronologia 28, 99-130.

docs.title: write_tridas
docs.text:
Write a TRiDaS 1.2.2 file from ring widths and/or a chronology.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default fname str

output path. .xml is appended if no extension is given.

required rwl pandas DataFrame

ring widths (Year-indexed, series in columns), as from dpl.readers(). Written as measurementSeries under one object (site).

None crn pandas DataFrame

a chronology from dpl.chron(); columns named samp_depth carry sample depth and pair with the preceding chronology column. Written as derivedSeries, unitless, with sample depth as each value's count.

None metadata TridasMetadata or dict

project/site metadata. Mandatory fields missing with validate=True raise a ValueError naming them (type/investigator are filled with "unknown" where the standard allows).

None prec float

measurement precision in mm (0.001, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 1, 10, 1000). None (default) uses the precision rwl was read at (rwl.attrs["dplpy_precision"], when every series shares one); else millimetres without rounding (lossless; mixed precisions warn).

None ids pandas DataFrame

tree/core[/radius/measurement] grouping, as from dpl.read_ids(). Default: each series is its own element (tree).

None taxon str

taxon for the elements. Mandatory per the standard when writing rwl.

None variable str

the measured variable (controlled vocabulary).

"ring width" measuring_method str

free-text measuring method (mandatory per the standard).

"unknown" validate bool

enforce the mandatory-field set.

True

Returns:

Type Description str

the path written.

docs.title: TridasProject
docs.text:
Parsed TRiDaS file.

Attributes:

Name Type Description measurements dict of str -> DataFrame

Dated measurement series grouped into ring-width tables, keyed by "object | variable | unit | taxon". Each frame is Year-indexed with series in columns (the dplPy rwl shape) and carries df.attrs["kind"] = "rwl".

derived dict of str -> DataFrame

Chronologies (TRiDaS derivedSeries), keyed by series title. Each frame is Year-indexed with the chronology column and, when the file records per value counts, a samp_depth column; df.attrs["kind"] = "crn".

undated dict of str -> Series

Measurement series with no calendar years (floating series), keyed by series id. Position-indexed; feed these to dpl.xdate_floater().

metadata TridasMetadata

The full metadata hierarchy.

docs.title: rwl
docs.text:
rwl() -> pd.DataFrame

Return the single ring-width table, or raise if the file holds more than one measurement table (then use measurements).

docs.title: TridasMetadata
docs.text:
The project/object/element/sample/radius/series metadata of a TRiDaS file.

Project-level fields are named (they are the mandatory ones in Brewer's list and what a .crn-style export needs). The object hierarchy is kept as nested dicts under objects so the whole tree stays navigable without a deep class hierarchy. laboratories and extra capture the rest.

docs.title: read_pos
docs.text:
Read CooRecorder .pos file(s) into a PosCollection.

path may be a single .pos file or a directory tree (every .pos under it is read and stacked into one ring-width frame). Series are named by file stem.

docs.title: PosCollection
docs.text: Result of read_pos(): whole-ring widths plus the pieces a .pos file carries that a Tucson .rwl drops. Mirrors TridasProject's role for TRiDaS.

docs.title: Statistics & indices
docs.text: Descriptive statistics, agreement measures, sample-depth signal strength, and derived indices.

docs.title: stats
docs.text:
Summary statistics for each series in a ring-width dataset.

Reports, for each series, the columns 'first', 'last', 'year', 'mean', 'median', 'stdev', 'skew', 'kurtosis', 'gini', and 'ar1' (dplR's rwl.stats()).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default inp str or pandas dataframe

a data file (.CSV or .RWL) or a pandas dataframe imported from dpl.readers(). Series with no measured values are dropped with a warning.

required

Returns:

Name Type Description data pandas dataframe

one row per series. 'year' is the SPAN first..last in years (as dplR's rwl.stats), not the number of measured rings; the two differ for a series with interior gaps (see dpl.samp_stats() 'seg' for ring counts).

Examples:

>>> dpl.stats(data)
References

.. [1] https://opendendro.github.io/dplPy/reference/statistics/#stats

docs.title: samp_stats
docs.text:
Per-year sample-tracking statistics for a ring-width dataset.

For every year in the dataset this reports how many series are present and, across just those present series, their mean length and mean cambial age -- the num / seg / age columns of an ARSTAN "tabs" file.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default data pandas dataframe

ring widths, years as the index and series as columns (e.g. from dpl.readers()). Raw widths or detrended indices give the same result -- only the pattern of present/absent values is used.

required

Returns:

Name Type Description out pandas dataframe indexed by year with columns
  • samp_depth : number of series present that year (the sample depth; ARSTAN's num). An integer count.
  • seg : mean segment length of the series present that year, where a series' segment length is its number of measured rings.
  • age : mean cambial age that year, where a series' cambial age is the number of years since its first ring (year - first_year + 1).

Years with no series present get samp_depth 0 and NaN for seg / age.

Notes

seg counts a series' measured rings; age counts years since its first ring. The two differ only for a series with an interior gap (an unmeasured year inside its span), for which the tree still ages but the ring is not counted.

Examples:

>>> import dplpy as dpl
>>> data = dpl.readers("../tests/data/csv/file.csv")
>>> dpl.samp_stats(data)

docs.title: rwi_stats
docs.text:
Whole-record chronology signal statistics (rbar, EPS, SNR).

Computes the mean interseries correlation (rbar), expressed population signal (EPS), and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) over the entire record as a single-row summary. The non-running counterpart of rwi_stats_running(), which it calls with running_window=False; see that function for full parameter and statistic descriptions.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default rwi_data pandas dataframe

detrended ring-width indices (e.g. from dpl.detrend()).

required ids dict, pandas dataframe, or None

tree/core structure; see rwi_stats_running().

None period str

"max" (pairwise-complete overlaps) or "common" (complete rows only); case-insensitive.

"max" corr str

correlation type, "spearman" or "pearson" (case-insensitive).

"spearman" prewhiten boolean

prewhiten each series with an AR model before computing correlations (see rwi_stats_running()).

False min_corr_overlap int or None

minimum number of overlapping years for a series pair to contribute.

None zero_is_missing boolean

treat exact zeros as missing values.

True round_decimals int or None

decimal places to round the statistic columns to.

3 common_interval str, (int, int), or None

restrict to a common interval first (see rwi_stats_running()).

None ar_max

prewhitening controls (see rwi_stats_running()).

10 ar_method

prewhitening controls (see rwi_stats_running()).

10 first_aic_min

prewhitening controls (see rwi_stats_running()).

10

Returns:

Name Type Description result a one-row pandas dataframe of chronology signal statistics.

Examples:

>>> import dplpy as dpl
>>> rwi = dpl.detrend(dpl.readers("../tests/data/csv/file.csv"), plot=False)
>>> dpl.rwi_stats(rwi)
References

.. [1] https://rdrr.io/cran/dplR/man/rwi.stats.running.html .. [2] Wigley, Briffa & Jones (1984), J. Climate Appl. Meteor., 23, 201-213.

docs.title: rwi_stats_running
docs.text:
Running (moving-window) chronology signal statistics (rbar, EPS, SNR).

For each moving window along the chronology, computes the mean interseries correlation (rbar) and, from it, the expressed population signal (EPS) and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of Wigley et al. (1984), after dplR's rwi.stats.running(); rwi_stats() is the whole-record special case (running_window=False).

When tree/core IDs are supplied (see ids), correlations are split into within-tree (rbar_wt) and between-tree (rbar_bt) components, and the effective signal rbar_eff accounts for averaging multiple cores per tree via an effective cores-per-tree factor c_eff. c_eff is ARSTAN-style running effective replication: the cores of each tree present in the window, not counting a core whose within-tree correlations all fail min_corr_overlap. This differs from dplR's back-calculation of the core count from the number of valid within-tree correlations (0.5 + sqrt(0.25 + 2 n_wt)); the two agree for the whole record when every within-tree pair is valid and trees have at most two cores, and can differ inside running windows. Without IDs, every series is its own tree and rbar_eff == rbar_bt == rbar_tot.

Windows start at the first year and advance by window_length - window_overlap; a trailing remainder shorter than a window is not covered (dplR instead chooses the start that maximises coverage).

EPS = n * rbar_eff / ((n - 1) * rbar_eff + 1) and SNR = n * rbar_eff / (1 - rbar_eff), where n is the number of trees contributing to the between-tree correlations.

NOTE: no acceptance threshold (e.g. the frequently cited EPS > 0.85) is applied or implied here; that threshold was an illustrative example for SSS (see dpl.sss()), not a general criterion for EPS.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default rwi_data pandas dataframe

detrended ring-width indices (e.g. from dpl.detrend()), with years as the index and series as columns.

required ids dict, pandas dataframe, or None

tree/core structure used to split within- vs between-tree correlations. Either a dict mapping {series_name: tree_id}, a dataframe with a 'tree' column indexed by series name (such as produced by dpl.read_ids()), or None to treat every series as its own tree (one core per tree).

None period str

"max" uses each pair's own overlapping years (pairwise-complete); "common" restricts each window to years present in every series that has data in the window (case-insensitive).

"max" corr str

correlation type, "spearman" or "pearson" (case-insensitive).

"spearman" prewhiten boolean

prewhiten each series with an AR model before computing correlations, using the package-standard autoreg._prewhiten() (Yule-Walker, order by the first local AIC minimum up to ar_max, ARSTAN backcast initials so no years are lost). NOTE: R's ar() / dplR take the global AIC minimum up to floor(10*log10(n)); pass first_aic_min=False for that rule.

False running_window boolean

if False, a single window spanning the whole record is used (this is what rwi_stats() invokes).

True window_length int or None

length of each moving window in years (None: min(50, n_years)).

50 window_overlap int or None

number of years successive windows overlap; defaults to window_length // 2.

None min_corr_overlap int or None

minimum number of overlapping years required for a series pair to contribute a correlation; defaults to min(30, window_length).

None zero_is_missing boolean

treat exact zeros as missing values (a zero RWI is treated as absent).

True round_decimals int or None

decimal places to round the real-valued statistic columns to; None leaves them unrounded.

3 common_interval str, (int, int), or None

restrict the data to a common interval before computing statistics. 'series', 'years' or 'both' selects a complete overlap-only rectangle via dpl.common_interval() (maximising cores, years, or cells); a (start_year, end_year) pair restricts to that inclusive span. None (default) uses the full record. Recommended for unevenly-distributed data, where period='common' on the full record can be empty.

None ar_max int

maximum AR order for prewhiten=True.

10 ar_method (yw, burg, ols)

AR estimator for prewhiten=True (case-insensitive).

"yw" first_aic_min boolean

AR order rule for prewhiten=True: first local AIC minimum (True) or global minimum (False, R's ar()).

True

Returns:

Name Type Description result pandas dataframe with one row per window (or a single row if

running_window=False). Columns: start_year, mid_year, end_year (running only), n_cores, n_trees, n, n_tot, n_wt, n_bt, rbar_tot, rbar_wt, rbar_bt, c_eff, rbar_eff, eps, snr.

Examples:

>>> import dplpy as dpl
>>> rwi = dpl.detrend(dpl.readers("../tests/data/csv/file.csv"), plot=False)
>>> dpl.rwi_stats_running(rwi, window_length=60, window_overlap=30)
References

.. [1] https://rdrr.io/cran/dplR/man/rwi.stats.running.html .. [2] Wigley, Briffa & Jones (1984), J. Climate Appl. Meteor., 23, 201-213. .. [3] Buras (2017), Dendrochronologia, 44, 130-132. .. [4] https://opendendro.github.io/dplPy/reference/statistics/#rwi_stats_running

docs.title: sens1
docs.text:
Mean sensitivity (dplR sens1).

The standard measure of year-to-year variability in dendrochronology (Douglass; Eq. 1 of Biondi and Qeadan 2008), typically computed on detrended series. For a single series of n (non-missing) values,

sens1 = (2 / (n - 1)) * sum_i |x_i - x_{i-1}| / (x_i + x_{i-1})

where a 0/0 term from an x_i + x_{i-1} == 0 pair is skipped while n - 1 is unchanged.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default data pandas.DataFrame, pandas.Series, 1-D array-like, or str

A ring-width dataset (years x series), a single series, or a path/URL to a .csv/.rwl file. NA/NaN values are dropped before the calculation.

required

Returns:

Type Description float or Series

For a single series, the scalar mean sensitivity. For a DataFrame (or a file path, which is read into one), a Series of the statistic indexed by series name. A series with fewer than two values yields NaN.

Examples:

>>> dpl.sens1(data)
>>> dpl.sens1(data["CAM011"])
References

.. [1] Biondi, F. and Qeadan, F. (2008) Inequality in paleorecords. Ecology 89, 1056-1067. .. [2] https://opendendro.github.io/dplPy/reference/statistics/#sens1

docs.title: sens2
docs.text:
Mean sensitivity for a series with a trend (dplR sens2).

Eq. 2 of Biondi and Qeadan (2008): the local two-year denominator of sens1() is replaced by the series mean, so a growth trend does not inflate the statistic. For a single series of n (non-missing) values,

sens2 = sum_i |x_{i+1} - x_i| / (sum(x) - sum(x)/n)
      = sum_i |x_{i+1} - x_i| / ((n - 1) * mean(x))

A series whose values sum to zero has no defined sens2 and yields NaN.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default data pandas.DataFrame, pandas.Series, 1-D array-like, or str

A ring-width dataset (years x series), a single series, or a path/URL to a .csv/.rwl file. NA/NaN values are dropped before the calculation.

required

Returns:

Type Description float or Series

A scalar for a single series, or a Series indexed by series name for a DataFrame / file path. Fewer than two values yields NaN.

Examples:

>>> dpl.sens2(data)
>>> dpl.sens2(data["CAM011"])
References

.. [1] Biondi, F. and Qeadan, F. (2008) Inequality in paleorecords. Ecology 89, 1056-1067. .. [2] https://opendendro.github.io/dplPy/reference/statistics/#sens2

docs.title: glk
docs.text:
Gleichlaeufigkeit (sign-agreement) between all pairs of series.

For every pair of series this is the proportion of shared intervals in which the two move in the same direction, counting a flat (no-change) interval as half agreement. A port of dplR's glk (Visser's implementation).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default data DataFrame or str

A ring-width dataset (years x series), or a path/URL to a .csv/.rwl file.

required overlap int

Minimum number of overlapping growth-change intervals a pair must share; pairs below this are NaN. Must be a single integer >= 3. A warning is issued for values below 50 (matches likely become statistically insignificant).

50 prob bool

If True, also return a matrix of two-sided p-values.

True

Returns:

Type Description dict of pandas.DataFrame

glk_mat (the statistic, diagonal set to 1), overlap (the number of overlapping intervals per pair), and, when prob is True, p_mat (two-sided p-values). All are n x n, indexed by series name.

See Also
