sgc : the synchronous / semi-synchronous decomposition (glk = sgc + ssgc/2).

Examples:

>>> res = dpl.glk(data)
>>> res["glk_mat"]
References

.. [1] Schweingruber, F.H. (1988) Tree Rings. Kluwer. .. [2] Visser, R.M. (2021) On the similarity of tree-ring patterns: Journal of Archaeological Science 125. .. [3] https://opendendro.github.io/dplPy/reference/statistics/#glk

docs.title: sgc
docs.text:
Synchronous and semi-synchronous growth changes between all pairs.

A decomposition of glk(): sgc is the proportion of shared intervals in which two series move in the same direction, and ssgc the proportion in which exactly one is flat. A port of dplR's sgc.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default data DataFrame or str

A ring-width dataset (years x series), or a path/URL to a .csv/.rwl file.

required overlap int

Minimum overlapping intervals per pair (a single integer >= 3); pairs below this are NaN. A warning is issued below 50.

50 prob bool

If True, also return a matrix of two-sided p-values (computed from sgc).

True

Returns:

Type Description dict of pandas.DataFrame

sgc_mat, ssgc_mat, overlap, and, when prob is True, p_mat -- all n x n, indexed by series name. (dplPy uses the *_mat keys in both branches; dplR's prob=False list names them sgc/ssgc -- the values are identical.)

See Also

glk : the combined statistic, glk = sgc + ssgc/2.

Examples:

>>> res = dpl.sgc(data)
>>> res["sgc_mat"], res["ssgc_mat"]
References

.. [1] Visser, R.M. (2021) On the similarity of tree-ring patterns: Journal of Archaeological Science 125. .. [2] https://opendendro.github.io/dplPy/reference/statistics/#sgc

docs.title: sss
docs.text:
Subsample signal strength (SSS) as a per-year series.

For each year, computes how well the subsample of series present that year represents the full N-series chronology (Wigley et al. 1984):

SSS(t) = n(t) * (1 + (N - 1) * rbar) / (N * (1 + (n(t) - 1) * rbar))

where N is the total number of trees in the record, rbar is the effective mean interseries correlation (both fixed, from a whole-record dpl.rwi_stats() call), and n(t) is the number of trees (or cores, if no tree IDs are given) present in year t. Mirrors dplR's sss(), holding rbar and N constant while only the per-year sample depth varies -- distinct from the running EPS of dpl.rwi_stats_running(), which recomputes rbar in each window.

No acceptance threshold is applied; SSS is the statistic Wigley et al. (1984) intended for assessing declining reconstruction skill back in time (the frequently cited 0.85 value was an illustrative example, not a rule).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default rwi_data pandas dataframe

detrended ring-width indices (e.g. from dpl.detrend()), years as index and series as columns.

required ids dict, pandas dataframe, or None

tree/core structure (see dpl.rwi_stats() / dpl.read_ids()). When given, both N and the per-year sample depth are counted in trees; when None, every series is its own tree and they are counted in cores.

None corr str

correlation type used for the underlying rbar ("spearman" or "pearson", case-insensitive).

"spearman" zero_is_missing boolean

treat exact zeros as missing (applied consistently to the rbar calculation and the per-year sample-depth count).

True common_interval str, (int, int), or None

restrict to a common interval before computing SSS: 'series', 'years' or 'both' selects one via dpl.common_interval(), and a (start_year, end_year) pair restricts to that span. rbar, N, n(t) and the returned years are then all taken from that trimmed block. None (default) uses the full record.

None

Returns:

Name Type Description result pandas Series named "sss", indexed by year, with the per-year subsample

signal strength (over the common interval if one was chosen).

Examples:

>>> import dplpy as dpl
>>> rwi = dpl.detrend(dpl.readers("../tests/data/csv/file.csv"), plot=False)
>>> dpl.sss(rwi)
References

.. [1] https://rdrr.io/cran/dplR/man/sss.html .. [2] Wigley, Briffa & Jones (1984), J. Climate Appl. Meteor., 23, 201-213. .. [3] Buras (2017), Dendrochronologia, 44, 130-132. .. [4] https://opendendro.github.io/dplPy/reference/statistics/#sss

docs.title: tree_mean
docs.text:
Average each tree's cores into a single tree-level series (dplR treeMean).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default rwl DataFrame

A ring-width dataset (years x cores/series).

required ids DataFrame or dict

The tree/core structure that says which tree each series belongs to -- the output of read_ids() (a DataFrame indexed by series name with a tree column), or a plain {series_name: tree_id} dict. Series are matched to trees by name, so ids need not be in column order.

required na_rm bool

If False (dplR's default), a tree's value for a year is NaN unless every one of its cores has a measurement that year. If True, the mean is taken over whatever cores are present (a year is NaN only when the tree has no core at all that year).

False

Returns:

Type Description DataFrame

A ring-width dataset (years x trees). Columns are the unique tree IDs, in order of first appearance among the input columns; the year index is preserved, and the input's provenance attrs are carried over (the output is still raw widths, kind="rwl"). Feed it straight to detrend() / chron().

Examples:

>>> ids = dpl.read_ids(data)
>>> dpl.tree_mean(data, ids)
>>> dpl.chron(dpl.tree_mean(dpl.detrend(data), ids, na_rm=True))
References

.. [1] https://opendendro.github.io/dplPy/reference/statistics/#tree_mean

docs.title: common_interval
docs.text:
Select a complete common interval from a set of ring-width series.

Finds the largest block of years and series in which every retained series has a value for every retained year (a complete, gap-free rectangle) -- the interval over which chronology statistics such as rbar, EPS and SSS can be computed without missing values. Ported from dplR's common.interval().

Three strategies trade off the number of series against the number of years:

  • "series" maximises the number of series (cores) at the highest sample depth -- typically a short, deep interval.
  • "years" maximises the number of years, dropping short series to extend the span -- typically a long, shallow interval.
  • "both" (default) maximises the number of data cells (series x years), a balance of the two.

To use an interval of your own choosing, slice the frame (e.g. rwi.loc[1800:1980]) before passing it on.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default rwl DataFrame

ring-width series (raw or detrended), years as the index, series as columns.

required type (series, years, both)

the selection strategy described above (case-insensitive).

"series" plot bool

if True, draw a coverage diagram (each series as a grey span, with the retained common interval overlaid in black).

False

Returns:

Type Description DataFrame

the trimmed frame containing only the retained series and years (a complete rectangle), carrying the input's attrs. The full frame is returned unchanged if no trimming is possible/needed.

Examples:

>>> import dplpy as dpl
>>> rwi = dpl.detrend(dpl.readers("../tests/data/csv/co021.csv"), plot=False)
>>> ci = dpl.common_interval(rwi, type="both")
>>> dpl.rwi_stats(ci)
References

.. [1] https://rdrr.io/cran/dplR/man/common.interval.html .. [2] Bunn (2008), Dendrochronologia, 26, 115-124.

docs.title: bai_out
docs.text:
Basal area increment computed from the outside in (dplR bai.out).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default rwl DataFrame

Year-indexed ring widths (one column per series).

required diam DataFrame, dict, or pandas.Series

Stem diameter for each series, in the same length units as the ring widths. A DataFrame uses a series column (or the first column) for the names and a diam column (or the second column) for the diameters; a dict/Series maps series name -> diameter. If omitted, each series' radius is taken as the sum of its ring widths (diameter = twice that).

None

Returns:

Type Description DataFrame

BAI in squared length units, same shape/index as rwl (NaN where ring width was missing), tagged attrs["kind"] = "bai". A warning names any series whose supplied diam is smaller than twice its summed ring widths: the radius then goes negative inside the stem and the innermost BAI values are negative (dplR behaves the same, silently).

docs.title: bai_in
docs.text:
Basal area increment computed from the pith out (dplR bai.in).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default rwl DataFrame

Year-indexed ring widths (one column per series).

required d2pith DataFrame, dict, or pandas.Series

Distance from the innermost measured ring to the pith, per series, in the same length units as the ring widths. A DataFrame uses a series column (or the first column) for the names and a d2pith column (or the second column) for the offsets; a dict/Series maps series name -> offset. If omitted, every offset is 0 (the innermost ring is assumed to reach the pith).

None

Returns:

Type Description DataFrame

BAI in squared length units, same shape/index as rwl (NaN where ring width was missing), tagged attrs["kind"] = "bai".

docs.title: Utilities
docs.text: Gap infilling, pith-offset conversion, LiPD interchange, plotting, and CLI helpers.

docs.title: fill_internal
docs.text:
Fill interior gaps (interior NaN) in a ring-width dataset.

Only interior NaN -- those between a series' first and last real ring -- are filled; leading and trailing NaN are left untouched. A real 0 (a locally absent ring) is data and is never treated as a gap. Series with one or no real value are returned unchanged.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default data pandas dataframe

ring widths (or indices), years as the index and series as columns.

required fill (Mean, Spline, Linear, ARSTAN)

how to fill each interior gap (case-insensitive):

  • "Mean" : the series' mean (flat fill).
  • "Linear" : straight-line interpolation between the flanking values.
  • "Spline" : cubic-spline interpolation through the present values. A spline can overshoot below zero next to a small ring; such values are clipped to 0 (a ring width cannot be negative) and the series named in a warning, so the fill can be reviewed.
  • a number : that constant value.
  • "ARSTAN" : impute each missing ring from the common (mean) chronology signal, moment-matched to the series and modulated by its growth curve (see Notes and _fill_arstan).

"Mean", "Linear" and "Spline" port dplR's fill.internal.NA() and interpolate within each series only.

"Mean" **kwargs

for fill="ARSTAN", forwarded to _fill_arstan (e.g. growth_nyrs, long_gap, flank).

{}

Returns:

Name Type Description out pandas dataframe, same shape/index/columns as `data`, with interior

gaps filled. The input's attrs (metadata, precision, provenance) are kept: the result is still raw widths.

Notes

The simple methods know nothing about the other series -- they just bridge each hole -- so use them when you need an NaN-free series for a downstream step, not as if the filled values were measured. "ARSTAN" instead borrows the shared year-to-year signal from all series.

References

.. [1] https://opendendro.github.io/dplPy/reference/utilities/#fill_internal

docs.title: edit_rwl
docs.text:
Insert, delete, or change one ring in a single series.

Returns a new object; the input is never modified in place (unlike the old Fortran programs, where the edit mutated the record). Assign the result to keep it. The fix that pairs with the crossdating checks: xdate, series_corr, and check find a misdated ring (a NEGATIVE lag there means a MISSING ring, so action="insert"), and edit_rwl corrects it.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default data DataFrame or Series

a ring-width collection (then series names the column to edit) or a single year-indexed series. Leading/trailing NaN rows of a Series are kept.

required series str or None

the series (column) to edit; required when data is a DataFrame.

None year int

the calendar year to act on (a whole number; NaN or 2003.7 is an error). For action="insert" it may also be the year just before the series (prepend).

None action (insert, delete, change)

"insert" adds a ring (a missed ring), "delete" removes one (a false or double-counted ring), "change" replaces a measured value without changing the series length or dating. Case-insensitive.

"insert" value float or None

the ring width, a finite non-negative number. Required for "change"; for "insert" it defaults to the series mean; ignored for "delete".

None fix_last bool

insert/delete only. True keeps the most recent year dated and lets the one-ring change roll off the inner (oldest) end; False keeps the inner end dated and changes the recent end. Matches dplR's fix.last.

True fix_length bool or None

insert/delete on a Series only. True (the default for a Series, as dplR's fix.length) keeps the series' original length by dropping (insert) or NA-padding (delete) one ring at the end opposite fix_last; a warning names the measured ring an insert drops. For a DataFrame it is not applied, following dplR's rwl method: no measurement is ever discarded, the collection simply gains a year (insert) or the series loses one (delete), and all-NaN rows a delete leaves at either end are trimmed. Passing fix_length=True with a DataFrame is an error, as in dplR.

None

Returns:

Type Description DataFrame or Series

a copy with the one edit applied, same type as data. For a DataFrame the edited column is realigned onto the (possibly one-year-extended) year index and the other series are untouched. The input's attrs are kept (the result is still raw widths).

Examples:

>>> import dplpy as dpl
>>> rwl = dpl.readers("co021.rwl")
>>> fixed = dpl.edit_rwl(rwl, series="641114", year=1900, action="insert")
>>> fixed = dpl.edit_rwl(rwl, series="641114", year=1905, action="delete")
>>> fixed = dpl.edit_rwl(rwl, series="641114", year=1912, action="change", value=0.44)
References

.. [1] https://rdrr.io/cran/dplR/man/insert.ring.html .. [2] https://opendendro.github.io/dplPy/reference/utilities/#edit_rwl

docs.title: po_to_wc
docs.text:
Convert pith offset to (partial) wood completeness (dplR's po.to.wc()).

The number of missing heartwood rings equals the pith offset (dplPy's pith offset is itself the count of rings between pith and first measured ring; 0 = pith present).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default po DataFrame

pith-offset table with a series column (series IDs) and a pith_offset column (integer rings between the pith and the first measured ring; 0 = pith present).

required

Returns:

Type Description DataFrame

one column, n_missing_heartwood (integer), indexed by series.

References

.. [1] https://rdrr.io/cran/dplR/man/po.to.wc.html

docs.title: wc_to_po
docs.text:
Convert wood completeness to pith offset (dplR's wc.to.po()).

The pith offset is the number of missing heartwood rings plus the number of unmeasured inner rings (0 = pith present), for every series whose pith presence is known (complete/incomplete) or whose missing-heartwood count is given; other series get a missing pith offset.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default wc DataFrame

wood-completeness table indexed by series, with any of the optional columns pith_presence ("complete"/"incomplete"), n_missing_heartwood (int) and n_unmeasured_inner (int).

required

Returns:

Type Description DataFrame

a pith-offset table with series and pith_offset columns (nullable integer; 0 = pith present), suitable as input to RCS.

References

.. [1] https://rdrr.io/cran/dplR/man/wc.to.po.html

docs.title: yrs_to_pith
docs.text:
Estimate years (rings) to pith from an estimated distance to pith.

Ports modendro's yrs_to_pith() (C. Maher). The number of unmeasured rings between the pith and the innermost measured ring is estimated as the distance to pith divided by a mean innermost ring width, rounded to a whole number of rings. The distance to pith is whatever you measured (e.g. in CooRecorder, as returned by dpl.read_pos().attributes); only the table format matters.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default rwl DataFrame

ring widths, years as the index and series IDs as columns.

required d2pith DataFrame

one row per series, with a series column and a distance-to-pith column named d2pith or distance_to_pith (same units as the ring widths, typically mm).

required method (dist, rings)

"rings" divides the distance by the mean of the innermost n_rings ring widths. "dist" divides by the mean of as many innermost rings as fit within the distance (at least n_rings), which tracks a changing growth rate near the pith better.

"dist" n_rings int

number of innermost rings to average ("rings"), or the floor on the number averaged ("dist").

10

Returns:

Type Description DataFrame

columns series, d2pith, mean_rw, and pith_offset (the estimated whole-ring offset, 0 = pith present), ready to pass to dpl.rcs/dpl.po_to_wc as a pith-offset table.

docs.title: to_lipd
docs.text:
Write dplPy chronologies to a LiPD .lpd file.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default chron DataFrame

Chronology output from dpl.chron() or dpl.chron_ars() -- year indexed, with one or more chronology columns and, if present, 'samp_depth' (written as the count / sampleCount companion).

required filename str

Output path. .lpd is appended if missing.

required rwl DataFrame

Raw ring widths the chronology was built from. Written as a further measurement table, and -- if metadata is None -- used to auto-fill site metadata from its dplpy_metadata attrs.

None metadata SiteMetadata or dict

Site metadata for the geo block; defaults to what rwl carries.

None dsname str

LiPD dataset name; defaults to the filename stem (a purely-numeric name is avoided -- pylipd cannot resolve one).

None column str

The primary chronology column (written with isPrimary=True).

'std' chronologies None | 'all' | list of str

Which chronology columns to write. None writes just column; 'all' writes every non samp_depth column (e.g. std/res/ars from chron_ars); a list writes those columns. The primary is written first.

None stats DataFrame

Per-year running statistics (e.g. dpl.chron_stabilized(..., running_rbar =True)); a running-rbar column is written as RBAR on the primary chronology table and EPS is derived from it and sample depth (or taken from an EPS column if present).

None publication dict

Citation for the record: any of authors/author (str or list), doi, title, journal, year, url, citation.

None provenance str

Free-text description of how the chronology was built (detrending, AR, robust mean, ...). Stored on each chronology variable's description/notes and PaST long name.

None archive_type str

LiPD archiveType. Defaults to 'Wood'.

None

Returns:

Type Description str

The path written.

Notes

Requires the optional pylipd dependency: pip install "dplpy[lipd]".

docs.title: from_lipd
docs.text:
Read a LiPD .lpd file into dplPy-native objects.

Returns a dict with:

  • 'rwl' : the raw ring widths as a year-indexed DataFrame (series as columns), ready for dpl.detrend / dpl.chron, or None.
  • 'chronology' : the primary (headline) chronology as a year-indexed DataFrame (trsgi plus any count/RBAR/EPS), or None.
  • 'chronologies' : a dict of all chronologies found (keyed by a label such as 'standard'/'residual'/'arstan'), from measurement tables and/or model summaries.
  • 'metadata' : a dpl.metadata()-shape dict from the geo block.
  • 'dsname' : the LiPD dataset name.

Requires the optional pylipd dependency: pip install "dplpy[lipd]".

docs.title: lipd_metadata
docs.text: Read just the site metadata from a LiPD .lpd file, as a dpl.metadata()-shape dict. Requires the optional pylipd dependency.

docs.title: plot
docs.text:
Plot a ring-width dataset as a line, spaghetti, or segment plot.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default inp str | DataFrame

a file path to a .csv or .rwl file, or a dataframe from dpl.readers().

required type str

'seg' (coverage segments, one bar per series), 'spag' (spaghetti: each series offset vertically, black by default -- pass color= a colormap name to shade by first year), or 'line' (all series overplotted against year).

'seg' ax matplotlib Axes

draw into this Axes instead of creating a new figure. When omitted, a figure is created and auto-sized to the data.

None show bool

call plt.show() after drawing. Set False to keep the figure for saving or further editing (the returned figure is still fully drawn). Under a non-interactive backend (scripts, tests, CI) plt.show() is a no-op, so the figure is closed after showing to avoid accumulating open figures; the returned (fig, ax) can still be saved.

True **kwargs

passed through to the underlying plotter (e.g. zfac and color for the spaghetti plot -- color takes a colormap name like 'viridis'/'turbo' or a single colour like 'black').

{}

Returns:

Type Description (fig, ax) : tuple of matplotlib Figure and Axes

the figure and axes drawn on, so callers can save or restyle them. (Earlier versions returned None; the figure is now returned for reuse.)

Examples:

>>> dpl.plot(data)
>>> dpl.plot(data, type="spag")
>>> fig, ax = dpl.plot(data, type="seg", show=False); fig.savefig("seg.png")
References

.. [1] https://opendendro.github.io/dplPy/reference/utilities/#plot

docs.title: help
docs.text:
Print help for dplPy in the console.

With no argument, print an overview of every public function (grouped by task, each with the first line of its docstring). With a function name -- dpl.help("readers") -- or the function itself -- dpl.help(dpl.readers) -- print that function's live signature and full docstring. The listing is generated from the installed package, so it always matches the real API.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default name str or callable

A public dplPy function name ("readers", "dpl.readers") or the function object. Omit for the overview.

None

Examples:

>>> dpl.help()
>>> dpl.help("xdate")
